quizzes.question: Its primary headwater source is traditionally traced to glacial streams on Nevado Mismi in the Peruvian Andes, and near Manaus, its dark acidic Rio Negro meets the Solimões River without immediately mixing. Carrying more water than the next seven largest rivers combined, no bridges cross its main stem due to its extreme width and surrounding dense rainforest. For the point, name this world's largest river by discharge volume, which flows through Brazil.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River originates on Nevado Mismi in Peru, features the 'Meeting of Waters' near Manaus, has no bridges crossing its main stem, and holds the largest river discharge volume in the world.

quizzes.question: The centripetal form of this vector quantity is directed toward the center of curvature and is calculated as velocity squared divided by radius. According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, this property is directly proportional to net force and inversely proportional to an object's mass. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity over time, measured in SI units of meters per second squared.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is a vector quantity defined as the rate of change of velocity, measured in m/s², and related to force and mass via Newton's Second Law (F = ma).

quizzes.question: Known in Tibet as Chomolungma and in Nepal as Sagarmatha, the region above 8,000 meters on this peak is referred to as the 'Death Zone' due to extremely low atmospheric pressure. It continues to grow at roughly four millimeters per year as the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates collide, and it was first officially scaled by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953. For the point, name this highest mountain above sea level on Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is Earth's highest peak at 8,848.86 meters, known as Sagarmatha and Chomolungma, located in the Himalayas.

quizzes.question: The proportionality constant for this interaction was first measured experimentally in 1798 using a torsion balance by Henry Cavendish. In General Relativity, it is modeled not as a mechanical force but as geodesics following spacetime curved by mass and energy, while classical physics states it drops off with the square of distance. For the point, name this fundamental force that accelerates objects toward Earth's surface at roughly 9.81 meters per second squared.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force attracts mass and energy, governed by Newton's law of gravitation (measured by Cavendish) and described as spacetime curvature in Einstein's General Relativity.

quizzes.question: This city's administrative structure includes 23 Special Wards as well as western municipalities and distant island chains such as the Izu and Ogasawara Islands located on the Kanto Plain. Formerly a small fishing village named Edo, it was renamed in 1868 when Emperor Meiji relocated the imperial seat from Kyoto. For the point, name this capital of Japan, the most populous metropolitan area in the world.
quizzes.explanation: Tokyo, originally named Edo, became Japan's capital in 1868 and comprises 23 Special Wards on the Kanto Plain.

quizzes.question: The third of these statements notes that action and reaction forces act simultaneously on different bodies, while the second defines force as the rate of change of momentum. First compiled in the 1687 treatise Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica, their first principle is also known as the Law of Inertia. For the point, name these three fundamental principles of classical mechanics formulated by an English physicist.
quizzes.explanation: Sir Isaac Newton formulated the three fundamental laws of motion published in the Principia Mathematica in 1687.

quizzes.question: Accounting for approximately 20 percent of total global river discharge into the ocean, this body of water forms a famous confluence with the sandy Solimões River. Flowing eastward across northern Brazil to empty into the Atlantic Ocean, its immense volume and surrounding dense jungle prevent any bridge from spanning it. For the point, name this massive South American river.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River accounts for 20% of global ocean discharge from rivers and flows across South America to the Atlantic.

quizzes.question: C4 and CAM plants minimize photorespiration in hot environments during this process by utilizing PEP carboxylase prior to carbon fixation. Its light-dependent stage takes place in thylakoid membranes where water molecules undergo photolysis to release oxygen gas. For the point, name this biological process where autotrophs convert light energy, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose.
quizzes.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process in plants and autotrophs that converts light energy, water, and CO2 into glucose and oxygen.

quizzes.question: Located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range along the border between Nepal and China, this mountain was named in English after a British Surveyor General of India. It sits at an officially recognized altitude of 8,848.86 meters and experiences extreme tectonic uplifting due to colliding continental plates. For the point, name this summit, the highest peak in the Himalayas.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas along the Nepal-China border.

quizzes.question: The Calvin cycle during this process uses the enzyme RuBisCO, considered the most abundant enzyme on Earth, to fix inorganic carbon. Taking place within the chloroplasts of plant cells, its non-cyclic photophosphorylation generates ATP and NADPH. For the point, name this chemical process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
quizzes.explanation: Photosynthesis uses RuBisCO in the Calvin cycle within chloroplasts to fix carbon into organic molecules using solar energy.

quizzes.question: Its primary headwater source is traditionally traced to glacial streams on Nevado Mismi in the Peruvian Andes. Near Manaus, Brazil, the 'Meeting of Waters' occurs where the dark, acidic Rio Negro and the sandy Solimões River flow side by side without immediately mixing. Accounting for approximately 20 percent of the world's total river discharge into the ocean, no bridges cross the main stem of this rainforest waterway. For the point, name this largest river in South America by discharge volume.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River originates in the Peruvian Andes near Nevado Mismi, features the 'Meeting of Waters' with the Rio Negro, and is the world's largest river by discharge volume with no bridges crossing its main stem.

quizzes.question: Centripetal forms of this quantity act on an object moving in a circular path and are calculated as velocity squared divided by radius. According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, this vector quantity is directly proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass. On Earth's surface, the standard value for this rate of change due to gravity is roughly 9.81 meters per second squared. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is a vector quantity defined as the rate of change of velocity over time. It is measured in meters per second squared and is related to net force via F = ma.

quizzes.question: Known as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet, this mountain continues to grow at roughly 4 millimeters per year due to tectonic plate collisions. Above 8,000 meters, climbers enter a hazardous region known as the 'Death Zone' due to extremely low atmospheric pressure and thin air. First officially summited on May 29, 1953, by Sir Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay, it stands in the Himalayas along the Nepal-China border. For the point, name this peak that is the highest mountain above sea level.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha/Chomolungma) is the world's highest peak above sea level, located in the Himalayas and first scaled by Hillary and Norgay in 1953.

quizzes.question: The universal constant governing this interaction, denoted G, was first experimentally determined by Henry Cavendish in 1798 using a torsion balance. Einstein's General Theory of Relativity describes this phenomenon not as a traditional mechanical force, but as the movement of mass along geodesics in curved spacetime. Its magnitude between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. For the point, name this fundamental force that attracts objects with mass toward each other.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is governed by Newton's inverse-square law, constant G measured by Cavendish, and explained as spacetime curvature in General Relativity.

quizzes.question: Situated on the Kanto Plain, this city lies near a complex triple junction of tectonic plates, contributing to major seismic events such as a catastrophic 1923 earthquake. Originally a small fishing village named Edo, it was renamed in 1868 when Emperor Meiji moved the imperial seat here from Kyoto. Consisting of 23 Special Wards alongside western municipalities and distant island chains, its broader metropolitan area holds over 37 million people. For the point, name this capital city of Japan.
quizzes.explanation: Tokyo, formerly known as Edo, is located on the Kanto Plain and serves as the capital and most populous urban area of Japan.

quizzes.question: First published in the 1687 treatise Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica, these three physical principles form the bedrock of classical mechanics. The first principle introduces the concept of inertia, while the second defines net force as mass times acceleration. The third principle famously asserts that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. For the point, name these fundamental laws of motion named after an English physicist.
quizzes.explanation: Newton's Laws of Motion were compiled in his 1687 Principia and outline inertia, F = ma, and equal and opposite reaction forces.

quizzes.question: Carrying more water than the next seven largest rivers combined, this vast body of water lacks any main-stem bridges due to its extreme width and seasonal flooding. Its upper stretches in Brazil are commonly called the Solimões before meeting the dark waters of the Rio Negro. Originating high in the Peruvian Andes, it flows eastward across South America into the Atlantic Ocean. For the point, name this South American river with the world's largest drainage basin.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River flows eastward from Peru through Brazil to the Atlantic, carrying roughly 20% of global river runoff without any bridges spanning its main channel.

quizzes.question: C4 and CAM plants avoid photorespiration in hot environments by using PEP carboxylase to fix carbon prior to entry into the Calvin cycle. During its light-dependent reactions, photolysis splits water molecules within the thylakoid membrane to generate ATP, NADPH, and oxygen gas. The carbon fixation phase relies heavily on RuBisCO, often considered the most abundant enzyme on Earth. For the point, name this biological process in which plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
quizzes.explanation: Photosynthesis takes place in plant chloroplasts, utilizing light reactions and the Calvin cycle (featuring RuBisCO) to transform carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.

quizzes.question: Located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range along the border of Nepal and China, this peak was named in English after a British Surveyor General of India. Climbers traversing its South Col route must pass features like the Khumbu Icefall and the Hillary Step before reaching its highest ridge. Officially measured at 8,848.86 meters in elevation, it is recognized as the world's highest peak. For the point, name this famous Himalayan mountain.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest stands at 8,848.86 meters along the Nepal-China border in the Himalayas and is Earth's highest peak.

quizzes.question: Because it is a vector quantity, a change in direction alone at constant speed still produces a non-zero value for this variable. It appears as the variable 'a' in the kinematic equation v equals u plus a t, as well as in the net force equation F equals m a. Expressed in SI units of meters per second squared, it measures the rate of change of an object's velocity. For the point, name this physical concept.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is the vector quantity representing velocity change over time, measured in m/s² and related to force by Newton's Second Law.

quizzes.question: The primary headwater source of this body of water was traditionally traced to glacial streams on Nevado Mismi in the Peruvian Andes. Near Manaus, Brazil, its dark Rio Negro and sandy Solimões River flow side by side at the 'Meeting of Waters' without immediately mixing. For the point, name this massive South American river, the world's largest by discharge volume.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River originates in the Peruvian Andes near Nevado Mismi and features the 'Meeting of Waters' near Manaus, serving as the largest river by discharge volume in the world.

quizzes.question: Directed toward the center of curvature in circular motion, the centripetal form of this quantity is calculated as velocity squared divided by radius. According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, this vector quantity is inversely proportional to mass and directly proportional to net force. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity, measured in SI units of meters per second squared.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is the vector quantity representing the rate of change of velocity over time. It is measured in m/s² and related to force and mass via Newton's Second Law (F = ma).

quizzes.question: Known as Chomolungma in Tibet and Sagarmatha in Nepal, the region above 8,000 meters on this mountain is referred to as the 'Death Zone' due to extremely low oxygen levels. First officially summited in 1953 by Sir Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay, it continues to grow roughly 4 millimeters per year due to tectonic activity. For the point, name this Himalayan mountain that stands as the highest peak above sea level on Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha/Chomolungma) is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, first summited by Hillary and Norgay in 1953.

quizzes.question: The constant associated with this interaction was first experimentally measured in 1798 by Henry Cavendish using a torsion balance. General Relativity describes this phenomenon not as a standard mechanical force, but as objects following geodesics through curved spacetime. For the point, name this universal fundamental interaction that attracts bodies with mass to one another, causing objects on Earth to accelerate downward at approximately 9.81 meters per second squared.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is the fundamental interaction describing mutual attraction between masses. Its gravitational constant G was measured by Cavendish, and it is described by Newton's law and Einstein's General Relativity.

quizzes.question: Situated on the Kanto Plain near a complex triple junction of tectonic plates, this city was heavily damaged by a major earthquake in 1923. Originally a small fishing village named Edo, its present-day administrative structure comprises 23 Special Wards as well as distant island chains like the Izu and Ogasawara Islands. For the point, name this most populous metropolitan area in the world, the capital city of Japan.
quizzes.explanation: Tokyo (formerly Edo) sits on the Kanto Plain in Japan, features 23 Special Wards, and is the center of the world's most populous metropolitan area.

quizzes.question: The third of these statements notes that action and reaction forces act simultaneously on different bodies with equal magnitude and opposite direction. First compiled in the 1687 treatise Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica, the first of these statements is also known as the Law of Inertia. For the point, name these three fundamental physical principles formulated by an English scientist that describe how forces affect an object's motion.
quizzes.explanation: Newton's Laws of Motion describe inertia, force (F=ma), and action-reaction pairs, laying the foundations for classical mechanics in the Principia Mathematica.

quizzes.question: Carrying more water than the next seven largest rivers combined, no bridges cross the main stem of this waterway due to its extreme width and surrounding dense rainforest. This river accounts for roughly 20 percent of total global river discharge into the ocean as it flows eastward through northern South America. For the point, name this river that flows through Brazil, widely recognized as the second-longest river in the world.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River has no bridges spanning its main stem and accounts for approximately 20% of global river ocean discharge.

quizzes.question: Oxygen gas released during this metabolic process originates entirely from the photolysis of water molecules within light-dependent reactions. Carbon fixation during its light-independent reactions relies heavily on the enzyme RuBisCO within the Calvin cycle. For the point, name this primary biological process by which plants and algae convert light energy, carbon dioxide, and water into chemical energy in the form of glucose.
quizzes.explanation: Photosynthesis involves light-dependent photolysis of water and the Calvin cycle (using RuBisCO) to transform solar energy, water, and CO2 into glucose and oxygen.

quizzes.question: Named in English after a British Surveyor General of India, this physical feature is situated in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range on the border between Nepal and China. Standing at an officially recognized altitude of 8,848.86 meters, its extreme climate requires climbers to use supplemental oxygen in the Death Zone. For the point, name this peak in the Himalayas, the tallest mountain on Earth above sea level.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is located in the Mahalangur Himal on the Nepal-China border, named after Sir George Everest, and stands at 8,848.86 meters tall.

quizzes.question: In single-variable calculus, this physical concept is mathematically defined as the second time derivative of position or the first time derivative of velocity. On Earth's surface at sea level, standard gravity imparts an approximate value of 9.81 meters per second squared for this quantity on free-falling bodies. For the point, name this vector quantity that measures any change in an object's speed or direction.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is the second time derivative of position (or first derivative of velocity). On Earth, gravitational acceleration is roughly 9.81 m/s².
